summary: Alexander Pancoe, 31, of Chicago suffered a severe lower leg injury about 1,500 ft above Snowmass Lake on Snowmass Mountain and was left cold, wet and unable to descend after thunderstorms; ~20 Mountain Rescue Aspen members responded and a Blackhawk helicopter from the Gypsum HAATS site airlifted him at about 4:45 p.m. to Aspen Valley Hospital
location: Snowmass Mountain, ~1,500 ft above Snowmass Lake
responding_agency: Mountain Rescue Aspen + Colorado Army National Guard High Altitude Aviation Training Site
notes: Date inferred: Snowbrains article reports a Tuesday incident; article images and update stamp place publication in July 2018 (Sat 2018-07-21), so the preceding Tuesday is 2018-07-17. Pancoe was training for an Everest expedition; later reporting (Men's Journal 2025) confirms the 2018 Snowmass leg injury with frostbite Merged run 515: subject's own 14ers.com trip report (posted 2021-02-13; incident recounted as July 17, 2018) corroborates the Mountain Rescue Aspen + HAATS Black Hawk hoist — hoisted off the drainage below the summit ridge, flown to Aspen Airport, transported by ambulance to the hospital; injury was a calf laceration to muscle/tendons from a rock while descending snowfield near the summit ridge. | 2026-09-15: 14ers.com link removed per site ban; row retains other verified source(s). 2026-09-22: merged MRA FB post permalink (MRA Snowmass Lake Incident post: Alexander Pancoe, severe lower-leg injury ~1,500 ft above).
